Nothing to calculate yet. Add a saving below or set the time saved per day.
Off by default. Records anonymous performance data and crashes on this device only. Nothing is sent anywhere.

Each card is one thing you want to stay away from.

• The counter shows how long it has been since your last relapse. It is calculated from the saved time, so nothing runs in the background.
• Tap the card for a detailed summary with progress bars.
• Tap the priority to change it. Cards are sorted by priority.
• ↺ logs a relapse (or starts tracking again).
• ■ stops tracking. The time stays saved.
• Timeline shows all attempts.
• … opens daily notes, savings, display options and milestones.
• 🗑 deletes the entry for good.

Display options: choose whether the card shows the counter, a countdown to the next milestone, or both, and how exact the time is shown.

The chart button at the top opens your statistics.

Logging a relapse ends the current attempt and starts a new one right now. Your history is kept in the timeline.\n\nMoney and time spent are optional. If you enter them, they are subtracted from your savings, so the totals stay honest. Leave the fields empty if you do not want to track this.

Enter what you save by not doing it.

• Money: the amount and its currency. All money savings are added up and shown on the main screen, for this month and in total.
• Time: hours you used to spend on it (1.5 = one and a half hours).
• Other: anything you can count, for example cigarettes or drinks.

"Per" tells the app whether the amount is per day, per week or per month. The app converts it to a daily value and multiplies it by the time you stayed clean.

The name is optional for money and time. Without a name the category is used, e.g. "Money".

Here you see what staying clean has given you so far.

The totals are calculated like this: amount per day × the time you stayed clean, in all attempts together. Money and time you entered when logging a relapse are subtracted.

"This month" only counts the current calendar month.

Every saving has a category: money, time or other. Tap + to add one, the pencil to change it.
The timeline lists every attempt: when it started, when it ended and how long it lasted.\n\nThe hourglass button calculates the average length of the attempts you choose.
Milestones are goals such as \"7 days\" or \"3 months\". The bar shows how close you are, and the date shows when you will reach it.\n\nMonths and years follow the calendar, exactly like the counter.
Write down how a day went, what helped or what was difficult. There is one note per day.\n\nIf enabled in the settings, the app offers to write a note after a relapse.
The summary shows your current attempt with a progress bar for each unit of time.\n\nEach bar shows how far you are into the next unit, for example how much of the current day or month has passed.
Give the entry a name and choose when you stopped. You can choose a date in the past, or in the future if you want to start later.\n\nThe priority decides the order of the cards on the main screen.

When turned on, the app records anonymous technical data on this device:

• how long the app and each screen take to start
• how long loading and saving takes, and how many entries there are
• whether the counter updates run smoothly
• crashes (error type and code location only)

Never recorded: names of your entries, notes, amounts, dates of relapses, or anything that identifies you or your phone.

The log stays on your phone (max. 256 KB). It only leaves the phone if you export it and send it to someone yourself.

These options only change how the time is shown. The time is always tracked to the second.

• Shown on the card: the counter since your last relapse, a countdown to your next milestone, or both. Without milestones left the counter is shown.
• Number of units: how many units are shown, starting with the largest one you have reached. "1" shows only "2 years", or "5 hours" on the first day.
• Smallest unit: hides everything below, e.g. "Minutes" hides the seconds.

Example: number of units 2 and smallest unit minutes shows "5 hours 30 minutes" on the first day and "3 days 4 hours" later.
Add an entry to see statistics.

Current streak: %1$s

• Overview: how many relapses happened in each of the last 12 months, for all entries together.
• Per entry: your current and longest streak, the average length of finished attempts, the number of relapses and the time you stayed clean in total.
• The chart shows the length of the last attempts in days, the newest on the right.

Everything is calculated on your phone from the times you saved.
New entries get a set of milestones. You can remove them from an entry at any time.
Adds the default milestones to all entries that do not have them yet
Add the default milestones to all existing entries? Milestones they already have are kept.
Pure black backgrounds in dark mode. Saves battery on OLED screens.
Add, rename, sort and fill the tabs of the main screen
The first tab shows every entry
Tap \"Add\" to start tracking something you want to stay away from.
No entries in this tab yet.\nTap the ⚙ button on a card (or hold the card) to add it, or change the tab in \"Manage tabs\".
Delete the tab \"%s\"? The entries in it are not deleted.

Each card is one thing you want to stay away from.

• The ring fills up towards your next milestone. The number inside is the number of full days.
• Below the name you see the counter (or a countdown to your next milestone) and what you have saved.
• Tap the card for a detailed summary. Tap the priority to change it.
• Relapse logs a relapse; optionally with money and time spent.
• ⚙ (or holding the card) opens the display options: counter or countdown, how exact the time is shown, which buttons are visible and in which tabs the entry appears.
• The other buttons open the timeline, daily notes, savings and milestones, stop tracking, or delete the entry.

Swipe left and right to switch tabs. Tabs can be filled automatically (for example by priority) or by hand; see "Manage tabs" in the menu.

The chart button opens your statistics. Nothing runs in the background: the time is calculated from the saved timestamps.

Tabs group your entries on the main screen. Swipe left and right to switch between them.

• Fill automatically: the tab shows every entry that matches, for example all entries with high priority. New entries appear by themselves.
• Add by hand: tick the entries that should always be in this tab. You can also do this from the display options of a card.

Both can be combined. Use the arrows to change the order. The "All" tab can be hidden in the settings.

Appearance
Theme: light, dark, or follow the system setting.
Material You: uses the colors of your wallpaper (Android 12 and newer).
True black (AMOLED): pure black backgrounds in dark mode (new look only). Saves battery on OLED screens.

Layout (new look only)
Manage tabs: add, rename, sort and delete the tabs of the main screen, and choose how they are filled.
Show “All” tab: the first tab with every entry. Turn it off if you only want your own tabs.
Sort cards by: order of the cards inside a tab: priority, longest or shortest streak, or name.

General
Date format: how dates are written everywhere in the app.
Add note after relapse: after logging a relapse (or stopping), the app offers to write a note for today.
Number of Relapses: how many of the last finished attempts are used for the “Recent average” on the cards. 0 hides the average.

Timeline
Use alternative timeline view: shows the attempts as a vertical line with points instead of a list of cards.

Daily notes
Sort order: oldest or newest note first.

Milestones
Sort order: shortest or longest milestone first.
Hide completed milestones: milestones you have reached are no longer listed.
Default milestones: new entries automatically get a set of milestones (1 day, 1 week, 1, 3 and 6 months, 1, 2 and 5 years). On by default; you can remove them from an entry at any time.
Edit default milestones: remove milestones from the set, add your own, or reset to the standard set.
Add to existing entries: adds the set to all entries you already have.

Diagnostics
Collect diagnostic logs: records anonymous technical data on this phone to find problems. Off by default.
What is collected?: shows exactly what is (and is not) recorded.
Export diagnostic logs: saves the log as a text file, for example to send it to the developer.
Delete diagnostic logs: removes everything recorded so far.

Data
Export: saves all entries, notes, savings and milestones to a file. Do this regularly as a backup.
Import: adds the entries of an export file, for example from the original Sobriety app. Nothing is overwritten.
